cards.title: First to Solve It
cards.instruction: Treat each clue and inconsistency as a contest over who can understand the situation first and most completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've found the missing parcel's tracking error. Put my name beside it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were both looking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I circled it while you were saying looking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's fix it together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After recording who made together useful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've solved your missing parcel. Tracking says reception; you were still refreshing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for three boxes. Only two reached our office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then one stayed downstairs. I've narrowed your whole building to one desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The trolley's here. There's a box wedged underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So it left reception but never got unloaded. You've found the parcel; I've solved why we've been calling reception all morning.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 claim credit for an error, but A5 prioritizes recording credit over understanding more completely.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 counters B2's shared search; A5 makes B4's cooperative fix conditional on attribution.

relationship.evidence: B2 claims joint effort and B4 offers practical cooperation that A obstructs.

heightening.evidence: A5 repeats the credit demand without introducing another clue or a more complete explanation.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a missing parcel's tracking error and an immediate attribution dispute.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's circled-versus-looking line fits rivalry; A5's together-useful phrasing becomes abstract.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 contrasts A's claimed solution with B 'still refreshing'; A3 claims superior narrowing; A5 counters B's discovery by claiming the more complete explanation. Competitive understanding is clear, though A3's certainty outruns the evidence.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's three-box receipt and two-box arrival cause A3's downstairs hypothesis. B4's box under the trolley overturns that hypothesis, and A5 incorporates it into an unloading explanation while reclaiming credit.

relationship.evidence: B2 contributes delivery facts and B4 actually finds the box, pursuing parcel recovery rather than merely feeding boasts. A5 acknowledges B's achievement while competing over what counts as solving.

heightening.evidence: After B4 wins the physical search, A5 raises the contest from locating the parcel to explaining the morning's wasted calls. This develops the established competition, though chiefly through a verbal claim.

specificity.evidence: A1 immediately establishes parcel tracking and reception; B2 supplies the three-versus-two discrepancy; B4 reveals the box wedged under the trolley. Each detail gives actors a clear, playable discovery.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'one desk' makes premature certainty compactly comic. A5's distinction between finding and solving follows B4, although the final explanation is longer and more explicit than the earlier boasts.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 establishes a box missing between reception and the office; A3 uses that discrepancy to claim it stayed downstairs.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 locates the box under the trolley, forcing A5 to abandon the downstairs claim and compete instead over explaining why it remained missing.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 repeatedly turn parcel evidence into claims of intellectual precedence or completeness, directed at the colleague making competing discoveries.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 responds to losing the search by claiming a broader explanatory victory. Finding the parcel resolves a fictional problem without prescribing an ending for the actual scene.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A treats understanding each clue first and extending that understanding furthest as a competition.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Credit seeking wants recognition for a contribution; this card makes continuing interpretation itself the race.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A3 interprets B2's unequal box counts as a location; A5 uses B4's trapped box to replace that theory with a failed-unloading explanation and claim fuller understanding than B's discovery.

records.recommendedEdit: Preserved the original firstPass exactly. Kept the office parcel search, replacing the date and proposed speakerphone race with box counts and a trolley carrying the missing box. The rejected A5 only promised understanding; the new B4 supplies physical evidence that A5 immediately uses to explain the failed delivery while maintaining superiority. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5 (A1 races B's refreshing; A5 claims explanation outranks discovery), logic 4 (B2's count supports A3's hasty location theory; B4's trapped box supports A5's unloading explanation), relationship 4 (B2 contributes the delivery discrepancy and B4 actively finds the box), heightening 4 (A5 absorbs the correction by expanding location into a causal account), specificity 4 (A1 tracking, B2 office delivery, B4 trolley), brevity 4 (A5's found/solved distinction follows the evidence): 86. Five spoken ABABA turns, 74 words, and causal gates pass. Separate internal model reread only; the transfer reservation remains unresolved.
records.remainingConcern: A3 makes an unsupported deduction, and A5's explanatory victory is slight because B4 has supplied the decisive evidence. These remain playable expressions of sincere competitive certainty. No rewrite is needed.
records.writerReservation: A3 mistakes an unaccounted-for box for proof it stayed downstairs; A5 also assumes the wedged box is their parcel before checking its label. These are visible competitive overclaims, and B remains free to correct them. The final line adds the morning's calls as shared search history.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved S130-single-b has B challenge successive mystery-judge deductions while A claims the fuller sequence. Here B independently recovers a real missing item, forcing A to concede the discovery and shift the criterion for victory to explanation.

cards.title: First to Solve It
cards.instruction: Treat each clue and inconsistency as a contest over who can understand the situation first and most completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mystery guest is the baker. I solved it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you about the flour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A clue is not a conclusion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said it was the baker.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but I believed it decisively.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our mystery judge is the baker. Flour on the invitation. Solved before you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The miller uses flour too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it's the miller. I've already moved past the obvious answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's icing on the envelope flap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The baker, licking it after decorating. I've got the identity and the sequence; you've got ingredients.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 declares a solved mystery, but A5 replaces being first or most complete with a claim to decisive belief.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 distinguishes B2's clue from a conclusion; B4 removes that defense and A5 invents a new one.

relationship.evidence: B2 claims the clue and B4 credibly corrects A's account of who named the baker.

heightening.evidence: A5 intensifies the self-serving claim but stops advancing understanding of the mystery.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies a mystery guest and B2 flour, without establishing the occasion.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's decisive belief is a compact response to B4, though it rewards credit grabbing over deduction.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims 'Solved before you'; A3 claims to be ahead despite changing answers; A5 contests completeness of understanding.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's miller possibility causes A3's switch; B4's icing causes A5 to return to the baker with an added sequence.

relationship.evidence: B2 challenges an inference and B4 supplies discriminating evidence, repeatedly threatening A's claim to superiority.

heightening.evidence: A5 responds to B4's better clue by claiming both identity and chronology, then reducing B's contribution to ingredients.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a mystery judge and flour on an invitation; B4 locates icing on the envelope flap.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's 'identity and the sequence' versus 'ingredients' turns B's useful clue into A's competitive accounting.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 identifies another flour user; A3 adopts that suspect while claiming the change demonstrates being ahead.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 adds icing on the flap; A5 restores the baker and invents a more complete account to reclaim superiority.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A treats every clue as a contest for first and fullest understanding, including evidence supplied by B.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A shifts the competition from naming the judge first to claiming the entire sequence of events.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A turns every clue and correction into a contest to reach the earliest and most complete explanation.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Professional suspicion delays action to investigate; competitive solving uses investigation to outrank another person's understanding.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A1 explicitly races B, and A5 claims both identity and sequence as superior to B's isolated clue.

records.recommendedEdit: Added a mystery-judge invitation while retaining baker and flour. Separate reread: fidelity 5 (A1 firstness and A5 completeness), logic 5 (B2 miller revises A3; B4 icing revises A5), relationship 4 (B contributes rival evidence), heightening 4 (A5 claims a sequence), specificity 4 (A1 invitation), brevity 4 (A5 ingredients comparison): 90. All dialogue gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: The licking-and-decorating sequence is speculative, but reads as A's competitive overclaim rather than an established deduction. No rewrite needed.
records.writerReservation: A's deductions remain overconfident: icing suggests a baker but cannot prove the proposed licking sequence.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b has an active evidentiary rival and explicit credit competition; a relies on cooperative confirmation and unexplained knowledge.

cards.title: Effortlessly Unbelievable
cards.instruction: Be sincerely impressed by how naturally someone inhabits the strange reality, then compete to appear even less surprised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A talking doorway? How ordinary. I speak fluent hinge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You look amazed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only at how loudly it uses its indoor voice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Say something to it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely weather for opening. Completely natural conversation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asked that talking doorway for directions without hesitating. That's impressive. I usually just chat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then ask it where the toilets are. We're late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Morning, door. Usual question: toilets?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Through its ear. Give me a minute; I've never gone in that way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Left ear or right, door? You take your minute. I'll save you a cubicle.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims fluent hinge, but no turn expresses sincere admiration for B's ease with the strange reality.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's accusation of amazement; A5 responds to B4's request to address the doorway.

relationship.evidence: B2 diagnoses A and B4 tests A, without demonstrating the admired naturalness required by the card.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from claiming fluency to addressing the doorway, but does not clearly compete with B's demonstrated ease.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a talking doorway and A5 supplies a directly playable greeting.

brevityWit.evidence: A1's fluent hinge is vivid, while A5's 'Completely natural conversation' explains the intended attitude.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sincerely admires B's unhesitating conversation with the doorway, then immediately competes with 'I usually just chat.' A3 claims habitual familiarity; A5 treats entering an ear as routine while B4 hesitates.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 supplies the toilet question and urgency, which A3 incorporates as its 'usual question.' B4 supplies the ear entrance and personal hesitation; A5 asks which ear and offers to save B a cubicle. The doorway's answer is compressed into B4 but remains intelligible.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants practical directions because they are late, redirecting A's display into useful action. B4 admits unfamiliarity and asks for time, giving A5 an opportunity to combine helpfulness with competitive composure.

heightening.evidence: A3 merely speaks casually to the doorway; after B4 reveals the entrance is through its ear, A5 commits to going through ahead of B. The escalation moves from conversational familiarity to bodily participation.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes companions seeking directions from a talking doorway. B2 adds lateness and toilets; B4 and A5 make the impossible entrance concrete through an ear, a side-selection question, and a cubicle.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'Usual question: toilets?' efficiently performs familiarity. A5's ordinary offer to save a cubicle earns its humor from B4's extraordinary entrance, although 'Left ear or right' is a fairly straightforward normalization.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 tells A to ask where the toilets are because they are late. A3 asks that exact practical question while presenting it as a familiar ritual.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 identifies the ear entrance and requests a minute to adjust. A5 responds to both: asking which ear, granting the minute, and confidently proposing to proceed first.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1 explicitly combines sincere admiration with an immediate claim to greater familiarity. A3 and A5 sustain that competitive lack of surprise through increasingly strange circumstances.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: B4's hesitation enables A5 to surpass B's initial ease by treating physical passage through the doorway's ear as an ordinary toilet visit. The offer leaves further interaction available.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A sincerely admires B's ease with a talking doorway, then competes to appear less surprised by treating its stranger directions as an ordinary route choice.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Competitive generosity or devotion would demonstrate greater sacrifice; this card makes A surpass B's apparent ease in accepting strangeness.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A1 explicitly admires B's lack of hesitation; B4 needs time to absorb entering an ear, while A5 asks only which ear and offers to save a cubicle.

records.recommendedEdit: Replaced the rejected candidate's tooth payment, which made extravagance clearer than lack of surprise. The doorway and toilet errand remain; the new illustrative detail is access through the doorway's ear. B2 causes A3's direct question, and B4's unfamiliar route and requested minute cause A5's unhesitating route clarification and offer to go ahead. The saved firstPass remains exactly unchanged and rates the original. Separate internal reread under coach-1.0: fidelity 5 (A1 admires B's ease; A5 overtakes B4's hesitation), logic 5 (A3 asks B2's question; A5 uses B4's ear and minute), relationship 4 (B2 wants directions promptly but B4 needs time to adjust), heightening 4 (A5 moves from casual conversation to immediately accepting passage through the speaker's ear), specificity 4 (A1/B2 establish the errand; A5 supplies an ordinary route question), brevity/wit 4 (A5's cubicle offer treats the new impossibility as routine convenience); total 90. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words, and all hard gates pass. This is an internal model reread, with no live testing.
records.remainingConcern: A3's claim of routine familiarity is slight, and B4 compresses the doorway's answer into reported information. Neither breaks the causal chain. No rewrite is needed; this review assesses the supplied original.
records.writerReservation: The doorway's ear requires imaginative acceptance, but the dialogue does not require physical entry or define its anatomy. A5's practical helpfulness must retain the competitive contrast with B4's requested pause. The unchanged transfer still omits initiating admiration.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved S157-single-b uses social familiarity: B corrects A's mistaken greeting and introduces hospitality etiquette, while A expands intimacy with Martin. S157-single-a uses practical urgency and B's eventual hesitation, allowing A to demonstrate greater ease through helpful action. These differ meaningfully in tactic and pressure; the reference alternative is not scored.

cards.title: Effortlessly Unbelievable
cards.instruction: Be sincerely impressed by how naturally someone inhabits the strange reality, then compete to appear even less surprised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've greeted the invisible guest so casually. I do that constantly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You greeted the umbrella stand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're often close friends.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The guest is behind you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I knew. I was including their furniture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You greet invisible guests so easily. I wish I had your touch. Actually, I usually hug them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the umbrella stand. Martin's behind you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Martin! No formalities between us. Come for supper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I usually ask whether he can eat visible food first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, we can skip all that. Martin, help yourself from the fridge whenever. I'll get you a key.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 notices B's casual greeting but mainly boasts; A3 and A5 protect competence rather than clearly express impressed competition.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2's umbrella-stand correction and A5 incorporates B4's location correction into the furniture excuse.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 help locate the guest, though B's role stays limited to correcting A's mistakes.

heightening.evidence: A5 broadens the excuse to furniture but repeats A3's face-saving tactic without a new social commitment.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an invisible guest and B2 supplies a clear mistaken greeting target.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's close friendship with furniture is concise and A5 recalls it, although that callback dominates the card.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 admires B's touch then claims hugs; A3 and A5 cover uncertainty with increasingly effortless intimacy.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 identifies Martin behind A, prompting A3's greeting; B4's food check prompts A5 to dismiss preliminaries and offer unrestricted fridge access.

relationship.evidence: B2 corrects A's mistaken greeting and B4 offers considerate guest knowledge, exposing the gap A tries to surpass.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands A3's supper invitation into anytime food access and a house key to seem more naturally familiar than B.

specificity.evidence: B2's umbrella stand and named invisible guest make the correction playable; A5 supplies concrete household stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A1's 'Actually' reveals the competitive pivot; A5's key offer earns its excess from avoiding B4's careful questions.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 corrects the guest's identity and location; A3 immediately greets Martin as an intimate acquaintance.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 models a careful dietary inquiry; A5 bypasses such formality with open-ended household access.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A's initial sincere admiration becomes a contest to appear more at home with invisible guests than the knowledgeable B.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 turns performed familiarity into a consequential offer of a house key.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A admires B's social ease with an invisible guest and then competes by offering even more unhesitating familiarity.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Bluffing prior acquaintance can resemble the scene, but the card specifically starts from sincere admiration and escalates apparent lack of surprise.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A1 openly wishes for B's touch before claiming hugs; A5 overtakes B4's careful hospitality with fridge access and a key.

records.recommendedEdit: Kept the invisible guest and mistaken stand, adding explicit admiration and consequential hospitality. B2 lets A3 address Martin; B4's food check prompts A5's conspicuous refusal of formalities. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A1 admiration precedes competition), logic 5 (A3 uses identity; A5 uses food etiquette), relationship 4 (B protects guest comfort), heightening 5 (A5 offers a key), specificity 4 (A1/B2 locate a social visit), brevity/wit 4 (A5's access offer earns the escalation); total 93. Hard gates pass.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. A1's admiration must remain sincere so the scene does not become merely defensive boasting.
records.writerReservation: A1's pivot from admiration to boasting should feel sincerely competitive, without implying deliberate deception about Martin's existence.
records.alternativeComparison: Compared with a's coffee courtesy, b uses correction, hospitality and household access to give competitive ease a clearer cost.

cards.title: Ready on My Terms
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest, hopeful, or vulnerable only in forms that preserve your emotional safety.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk about the argument, but not the whole year tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole year matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It does. Tonight I can finish one sentence without leaving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where do we start?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With the argument, and permission to pause.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk about last night's rent argument, but not the whole year tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole year matters. You've been pulling away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It does. One question, and let me finish before you answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Were you going to move out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I packed a bag. It's still upstairs. Please let that be the whole answer for a minute.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 agrees to discuss one argument under a scope limit; A3 and A5 explicitly preserve the ability to remain and pause.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 acknowledges B2's whole-year concern while limiting capacity; A5 answers B4's starting-point question with topic and safety condition.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the broader history recognized, then B4 cooperates in finding a manageable start.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds permission to pause but mostly consolidates A1's existing boundary.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an argument discussion tonight, and A3's risk of leaving makes the immediate limit playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's single sentence and A5's permission to pause express the emotional condition without explanatory padding.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 limits the conversation's scope, A3 negotiates one uninterrupted question, and A5 discloses the packed bag while requiring a pause.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's year-long concern causes A3 to permit a question under safer conditions; B4's moving-out question elicits A5's concrete admission.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the sustained withdrawal addressed and B4 uses the negotiated opening to ask the consequential question.

heightening.evidence: A5 moves from procedural limits to admitting a bag remains packed upstairs, then preserves safety by limiting immediate follow-up.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes last night's rent argument; B2 supplies ongoing withdrawal and A5 locates the packed bag upstairs.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's short admission and request for a minute are economical and sincere, but the exchange offers little comic turn.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 insists the larger history matters; A3 acknowledges it and permits one question while controlling interruption.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 asks whether A intended to move out; A5 answers with the packed bag and negotiates time to tolerate that disclosure.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1, A3 and A5 each make openness conditional on a specific protection against emotional overload.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 increases the disclosure's stakes while retaining a narrower temporal boundary; the requested minute does not force the scene to end.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: D119 makes A agree to emotional openness only within conditions that preserve A's sense of safety.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Avoidance refuses engagement; A offers a limited, feasible form of engagement and specifies the protection it requires.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A3 limits the exchange to one uninterrupted answer; after B4 accepts and asks about departure, A5 admits packing a bag while requesting time before further discussion.

records.recommendedEdit: Revised the rejected ending so protected openness occurs in speech. Added a rent argument and possible move to the existing year-long dispute. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5 (A3 and A5 preserve safety while answering), logic 5 (B2's larger concern prompts one-question terms; B4's accepted terms and departure question cause A5's bag admission), relationship 4 (B2 seeks the broader truth and B4 accommodates limits), heightening 4 (A5 reveals an actual preparation to leave), specificity 5 (A1 rent and A5 upstairs bag), brevity/wit 3 (A5 is direct and playable but lightly comic); total 90. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; hard gates pass. Downstream attribution remains separately unresolved.
records.remainingConcern: This is stronger as a vulnerable dramatic exchange than as comedy. Its exact behavioral progression is clear enough to pass without a rewrite.
records.writerReservation: The scene is primarily emotionally tense rather than comic. Its revised transcript cannot replace the supplied versioned seed snapshot without a separate provenance decision.
records.alternativeComparison: This alternative negotiates scope and conversational turns under direct questioning; the door-seat alternative uses an available exit and reassurance to enable a voluntary admission.

cards.title: What Really Happened?
cards.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the parcel in a bag or a box? You've used both words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles before choosing the noun.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It had a rigid lid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Let's build the object before the story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For this missing-parcel form: was it a bag or a box? You've said both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think. I carried it by the handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles. Were they attached to fabric or cardboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cardboard. It had a rigid lid, too.

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Approve the Impossible Plan
cards.instruction: Get someone to formally approve a plan whose logic becomes stranger each time it is explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approve storing Tuesday's rain in this cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tuesday hasn't happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why we have room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens if it overflows?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll borrow a saucer from Wednesday. Sign here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As venue manager, will you approve storing Tuesday's rain in this cup? The wedding needs a dry lawn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tuesday hasn't happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. We'll catch the rain before it learns how to fall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have another wedding Wednesday. What if it leaks overnight?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll seal it with Thursday's drought. Sign for two dry weddings; I'll invoice the drought after it happens.

specificity.evidence: A1 supplies rain, Tuesday and a cup; the approving institution is left implicit.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'why we have room' turns the exact objection into a compact project advantage.

hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 introduces leakage and Wednesday's wedding; A5 supplies a seal and asks approval covering both events.

cards.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
cards.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You fold the moon; I'll stack these chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the crescent. It already suggests a crease.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why do you get chairs?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone must keep the achievable work moving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For tonight's courtyard film, you fold the moon; I'll switch off the lamps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the crescent. It already has a crease.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the lamps. You handle the sky.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do lamps, chairs and projector if you'll own the moon. Can I tell the audience we're waiting for your blackout?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assigns moon folding to B and keeps chair stacking; A5 defends that division when challenged.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's method question with a crescent crease; A5 addresses B4's complaint about the easier task.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 requests a method for folding the moon; A3 offers the crescent's supposed crease.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 reverses the assignment; A5 counters with additional practical duties and pressure to accept named responsibility.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A keeps the impossible task assigned to B while personally offering only reasonably achievable work.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 moves from casual delegation to bargaining and prospective accountability before the audience.

cards.title: What Rule Did I Miss?
cards.instruction: Find the hidden rule that makes the strange situation consistent, practical, or at least survivable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What keeps the soup inside that upside-down bowl?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've never seen it either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then turn the spoon over. Let's test which thing owns down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The soup followed the spoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Hold it over the sink while we learn the next rule.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What keeps the soup inside that upside-down bowl?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've never seen it either.

beats.text: Then turn the spoon over. Let's test which thing owns down.

beats.speaker: B

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'which thing owns down' compresses the hypothesis; A5's sink precaution earns its humor from the observed rule.

cards.title: Believe This with Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into treating your impossible explanation as the most useful version of events.

beats.text: Concrete traps it halfway across the road. Tell him we're planning a route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: His truck's blocking the road already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Ask him to lead slowly toward the empty plot. It needs a guide.

cards.title: There Is a Process
cards.instruction: Treat every favor, feeling, and urgent need as a request requiring terms, documentation, review, and approval.
